# Pḗgasos: the stories first, then the spelling

You cannot weigh an accent without knowing what it carries. Here is what **Pḗgasos** has been carrying.

## The Stories That Carry the Name

**Out of the Gorgon.** Hesiod tells it in four lines: when Perseus cut the head from Médousa, out sprang great Pḗgasos and the warrior Chrysaōr — her children by Poseidṓn.  The horse flew to the "immortal ones," and Hesiod already knows his office: "he lives in the halls of Zeús, carrying thunder and lightning for the counsellor.

**Bellerophōn's Gift.** The hero Bellerophōn, sent to Lykia with a letter demanding his own death, was ordered to kill the Chimaira.  Píndar sings how Athēnā appeared with a golden bridle — "take this charm for the horse" — and how, sacrificing to Poseidṓn the horse-breaker, Bellerophōn caught Pḗgasos at the spring of Peirene and from the air slew the fire-breathing beast.

**The Flight Too High.** Success bred the fatal wish: Bellerophōn tried to fly to Olympos itself.  Zeús sent a gadfly to sting the horse, and the rider fell back to earth to wander the Aleian plain alone — Pindar's model of hybris punished — while Pḗgasos continued upward to the stables of the gods.

## And Here Is What the Spelling Preserves

Against those stories, the attestation: **Πήγασος**, on the evidence Hesiod, Theogony and Pindar set down. The name means "Possibly from πηγή (spring) or a pre-Greek name".


## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Pḗgasos
- **ASCII form:** pegasos
- **Meaning:** "Possibly from πηγή (spring) or a pre-Greek name"
- **Domain of influence:** Flight, Inspiration, Freedom
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** Πήγασος
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 198 of 282

## The Name Travels

His name is the syncretism: Luwian pihassas, a storm-god honoured in Cilicia, meets the Greek horse — which explains why an earth-and-sea creature serves the sky god's bolts.  Rome made him a cavalry emblem and a favourite of coinage; Corinth stamped him on her silver for three centuries as the city's own beast, since Bellerophōn's Corinthian Peirene was his watering place.

## The Address It Earned

The temple of **Pḗgasos** stands at [/sites/pegasos/](/sites/pegasos/) — [lore](/sites/pegasos/lore/), [scholars](/sites/pegasos/scholars/), [patterns](/sites/pegasos/patterns/) — because a name carrying this much story deserves more than a parking page. What survives here cannot be shown in ASCII: a feature of the original that the fallback alphabet flattens. That is the Tier-1 test, and this name passes it without argument.

## The Sources Are Open

The myths above are retold from the temple's record; the primary voices are in the [Sacred Texts](/texts/): [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/). Nothing in this file outranks them.
